To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
S. cerevisia 424A(LN-HST) is the best ethanologenic microorganism for the production of biofuel from corn stover.

the three ethanologenic organisms tested in this work can ferment both glucose and cellobiose in the presence of xylose and that S. cerevisiaee 424A(LH-NST) is the only strain tested in this study that can ferment xylose in the presence of glucose at a rate and yield sufficient for industrial application.
the ethanologens tested in this work can ferment glucose from corn stover at 18% solids loading.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a consolidated bioprocess (CBP) for the production of ethanol from lignocellulosics.
identifying the most robust ethanologens for industrial-scale lignocellulosics-to-ethanol production.
the comparison of three ethanologenic microorganisms in their ability to ferment sugars from corn stover and their performance at high solids loading in a lignocellulosics-to-ethanol process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tested ethanogenic bacteria are not suitable for industrial production due to the inability to ferment xylose at high solids loading.
S. cerevisae 424A(LHN-ST) is the best ethanogenic organism for industrial production of cellulosic ethanol from corn stover.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the most important factor for industrial implementation is the robustness of the ethanologen to grow in the presence of lignocellulosics hydrolysate, which is the major bottleneck for the bacteria tested.
the most relevant ethanologen for the production of cellulosic ethanol from lignocellulosics is S. cerevisae 424A(LN-HST).

the three ethanologenic organisms are comparable in their fermentation performance in the co-fermentation and xylose-only fermentations in CSL, but 424A(LHN-ST) is the best ethanologen for xylose-only fermenting lignocellulosics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fermentation of lignocellulosics hydrolysates is not a simple extension of the fermentation of glucose or xylose alone.
the fermentation performance of ethanologens can be significantly improved when the fermentation is conducted on lignocellulosics rather than CSL media.

the fermentation performance of E. coli KO11, S. cereviae 424A(LHN-ST) and Z. mobilis AX101 is similar in a CSL-supplemented fermentation, while in the lignocellarulosic hydrolysates the performance is strain dependent.
